pricing: Free (unlimited workouts, 3 templates, no ads) + Strong PRO: US $4.99/mo (also $3.99 listed), $19.99/6 mo, $29.99/yr (also $23.99), Forever $99.99 (also $79.99). PRO paywalls unlimited templates, body-part measurements, all charts, plate & warm-up calculators, themes/icons.
platforms: iPhone, Apple Watch (watchOS 10+), Android phone/tablet/Chromebook; no Wear OS; no documented web logging
positioning: Minimalist, private, ad-free strength logbook ('Think less. Lift more.') with a mature Apple Watch app and no social/AI features.

features.how: Per-set weight + reps for weighted exercises; separate exercise types include assisted bodyweight, duration and cardio (distance/time). CSV export (6.2.x) columns: Weight (kg), Reps, RPE, Distance (meters), Seconds, Notes — i.e. weight, reps, distance, time per set. Exercise type is fixed per exercise (category).
features.user_feedback: App Store review (2023): some pairings are not allowed, e.g. weight + duration (weighted plank) — workaround is putting seconds into the reps field; exercise type cannot be converted later.

features.how: Tap the set number to open the Set Tag menu: Warm-up, Drop Set, Failure (tap again to untag). Warm-up sets are excluded from charts/metrics. 'Failure' means one additional rep was attempted and failed (5 reps + Failure = 6th rep failed; 0 reps + Failure = failed 1RM attempt).

RPE logged per set on a 6–10 scale with half steps; select the Reps cell and tap the RPE button on the custom keyboard (tap again to clear). No separate RIR field — help center gives an RPE→RIR mapping table (e.g. RPE 8 = 2 RIR, 9.5 = 0-1). RPE also editable on Apple Watch set screen.
features.user_feedback: Android Premium user (May 2026) asked for built-in RIR, goal sets/reps, rest, tempo, body-side and equipment fields per exercise (GP review).

features.how: During a workout each set shows the previous performance for that exercise (last time it was performed); the Apple Watch app also shows previous performance for the current set. Focus Metric compares today's metric to the last time the exercise was performed. No documented option to restrict 'previous' to the same template.

Templates carry their own weights/reps; after a template-based workout the 'Update Values Only' / 'Update Template and Values' prompt writes the weights and reps you used back into the template, so the next session starts from last values. No documented auto-fill of a blank set from history beyond the 'previous' display.

Three note types: Workout Notes (top of Log Workout screen, shown in History), Exercise Notes (via exercise ... > Add a Note, per workout) and Pinned/'sticky' notes (pin an exercise note; shown in yellow every time the exercise is performed, not in History). No length limit. No per-set notes documented.
features.user_feedback: Android user: replacing an exercise erases its notes and sticky notes (GP review, May 2026).

features.how: Supersets/circuits group exercises shown with a vertical line; the 'Next' button jumps to the next set in superset order (A1,B1,A2,B2…). iPhone: Add Exercise > multi-select > Superset; Android: ... > Create Superset and link with chain icon. Also available on Apple Watch (exercise ... menu).
features.user_feedback: Strong itself says the superset UX differs between iPhone and Android and will be unified later; reviewers call the UI dated vs Hevy (aitoolsbakery).

features.how: Drag and drop on the exercise name during a workout (phone); on Apple Watch reorder via ... on the Workout Overview screen.

Replace an exercise via the exercise More (...) menu; Apple Watch got a 'Replace exercise' option in 6.1.0 (Jun 2025). Separate 'Transfer Exercise Data' merges history recorded under the wrong exercise (same category only, irreversible).
features.user_feedback: Replacing an exercise drops its notes/sticky notes (Android user, GP review 2026).

features.how: PRO only. Tap the weight field on a barbell/machine exercise, then the plate-calculator button on the keyboard; shows the most efficient plates per side. Accounts for bar weight; default Olympic bar 20 kg/45 lb, bar type changeable per exercise in the ... menu. Not on Apple Watch; minor iOS/Android differences.
features.user_feedback: 2020 App Store review: limited to common bar weights (no 25 lb Smith bar option).

features.how: PRO only. Exercise ... > Add (or Update) Warm-up Sets batch-adds tagged warm-up sets for barbell, dumbbell and machine exercises; formula customisable in Settings (iPhone) or during workout (Android). Not on Apple Watch.

App Store lists support for multiple exercise types 'including Assisted Bodyweight and Duration Exercises'. How bodyweight enters volume is not documented; a weighted + duration combination is not supported per a user review.

No per-side (left/right) set logging documented. iOS has Settings > Bonus Options > 'Count Dumbbells Twice' which doubles dumbbell weight in workout volume and volume charts; on Android dumbbell weight is always doubled.
features.user_feedback: Android Premium user asked for a built-in body-side field (GP review, May 2026).

features.how: No tempo field in the documented set fields or CSV export columns; a 2026 Play Store review from a Premium user requests a built-in tempo field.
Start an Empty Workout or a Template from the Start Workout tab; after finishing an empty workout the app prompts to save it as a new template.

History > workout ... > Edit Workout to change sets, date and start/end time. To log a past workout: start a workout, ... > Adjust Start/End Time, turn OFF Automatic Timing and set times. 'Start History From' setting hides older history from stats without deleting it.

Custom numeric keyboard with RPE and plate-calculator buttons and a 'Next' key that advances to the next set (superset-aware); swipe-to-delete sets; full-screen rest timer option. Apple Watch: Digital Crown pickers, long-press menus, action-button set completion and an Apple Watch 'Button Repeat' toggle (6.3.3).
features.user_feedback: Widely praised as the fastest/simplest logging UI ('easy to use even when exhausted' – Lifehacker quote on homepage; GGR pros). 2026 fixes for stuck keyboard / RPE keyboard on iOS 27.

features.how: Default rest timer 2:00 starts immediately when a set is checked off; shown top-left of the workout screen, tap to expand to full screen to adjust or Skip; can be made full-screen by default. Can also be started manually.

Per exercise via the ... menu, with separate durations for Warm-up sets and Working (regular) sets. Timer sound and behaviour in Settings > Rest Timer. Apple Watch cannot change all timers of an exercise (iPhone changes sync).

Rest-timer notifications fire when backgrounded and can include next-set details ('simple timer mode'); several 2025–2026 releases fixed timer notifications (stale details, firing after workout end, background countdown).
Live Activity and Dynamic Island support for rest timers added in iOS 6.5.0 (12 Aug 2026); Android 6.2 release notes list 'Live Updates'.

Duration exercise type exists; Strong 6 release notes reference 'inline timers' vs a 'simple timer mode' and the homepage lists 'Custom Timers', but the exact stopwatch/countdown flow for timed sets is not documented in the help center.
Workouts are timed automatically ('Automatic Timing'); start/end time can be adjusted during or after the workout.
No documentation found on reminders or auto-finish for forgotten workouts.

'Templates' (formerly Routines) store exercises/sets; created via '+ Template', inside a folder, or 'Save as Template' from History / after an empty workout. Free tier limited to 3 templates; PRO unlimited. After a template workout you are prompted: Update Template / Update Values Only / Update Template and Values / Keep Original (prompt can be hidden). Template Search added 6.3.0 (Mar 2026).

Folders with drag-and-drop, collapsible; Archive folder for unused templates; example templates can be hidden (Settings > Bonus Options). Help article says folders are iPhone-only ('coming to Android soon').

No multi-week program library; only a few built-in example templates. App Store says it is optimised for progressive barbell routines like Starting Strength / StrongLifts 5x5 but you build them yourself.
No % of 1RM prescriptions, blocks or deload scheduling documented; Strong is described by itself and reviewers as a logger that does not build programmes.
No AI or algorithmic workout generation on Strong's official pages (research-based review, Sep 2026).

Homepage feature list mentions 'Workout Scheduling'; Workouts-per-Week profile/home-screen widget with weekly goal; Calendar widget (6.4.0) shows monthly workouts and weekly streaks. No help article describes planning workouts on future dates.
Template/workout ... > Share uses system share sheet with a link; recipient taps link to import (needs Strong installed and an account). Strong 6 changed link format — old links incompatible.
'Over 200 built in exercises' per help center (third-party claims of 300–450+ conflict with this).
Exercise Detail 'About' tab with video or image instructions plus step-by-step text; App Store: 'growing library of animated videos'.

Create custom exercises from the Exercises tab (iPhone: New; Android: ... > Create Exercise) or during a workout; rename custom exercises (6.1.0). Built-in exercises can be hidden (swipe left, iOS only) and restored via an old workout. Custom exercises unlimited on free tier (not on PRO list).
features.user_feedback: Review: unused custom exercises can only be hidden, not deleted; can't view/unhide hidden ones easily; can't change exercise type (App Store review 2023).

features.how: Exercises are categorised by body part (e.g. arms, back); primary/secondary muscle mapping not documented. Homepage mentions a 'Muscle Heat Map'.
Exercise categories include equipment-like types (barbell/dumbbell/machine per warm-up calculator doc), but an equipment filter in search is not documented.
Search bar in the exercise library; 6.3.2 (Apr 2026) added highlighting of matched characters and improved ranking.
App available in 11 languages (EN, FR, DE, IT, JA, KO, PT, RU, zh-Hans, ES, zh-Hant); no Polish. Whether exercise names are localized is not documented.
No next-weight/rep suggestions; 'Strong logs what you do, it doesn't tell you what to do next' (reviews). Focus Metric only compares against last session.
No progression rules engine documented.
No recovery/readiness or deload model documented.
No AI or coaching features found on official pages (Sep 2026).
No recovery/readiness/fatigue model; reviewers note no HRV/sleep/WHOOP/Oura integration and no recommendations.

Exercise Records tab: all-time bests (estimated 1RM, max weight, max volume) with history, plus best actual performance at each rep count next to a predicted value; only sets ≤12 reps count. History cards show number of PRs per workout. Best Set ignores 0-rep sets.
Brzycki formula; Strong warns estimates break down above 12 reps (records limited to ≤12 reps).

Exercise Detail 'Charts' tab (PRO only) with charts depending on exercise type (e.g. best set, 1RM progression, volume). Any exercise chart can be pinned to the Profile dashboard. Free users have limited charts.
Total workout volume and per-exercise volume charts (dumbbell doubling configurable); Focus Metric shows volume / % volume change vs last session. Weekly sets/volume per muscle group not documented.
'Muscle Heat Map' appears in the homepage feature list; no help-center documentation of how it works.

History has a calendar of workout days; Workouts-per-Week widget with goal (🎯) and optional 'Week of Year' labels (6.4.2); Calendar home-screen widget with monthly workouts and weekly streaks and an Activity widget (6.4.0, May 2026).
Finished workouts appear in History cards with duration, total weight, PR count and best set per exercise; prompts to save as template. No richer post-workout summary screen documented.
No strength standards / percentiles documented; Strong has no social or comparison features.

Measurements: Weight, Body Fat %, Caloric Intake (kcal) — all free and syncable with Apple Health (Google Fit/Health Connect on Android). Measurements can be added from Profile widgets (shortcut added 6.2.9) and exported to CSV (6.2.0).
PRO only: neck, shoulders, chest, left/right bicep, left/right forearm, upper abs, waist, lower abs, hips, left/right thigh, left/right calf.
App Store: 'Add notes and progress pictures to your workouts'; help center suggests taking progress photos. No dedicated photo-comparison feature documented.
No sleep/HRV/readiness inputs; reviewers note no recovery integration (WHOOP/Oura).

Profile > Settings > App Integrations > Apple Health > Connect (plus system permissions). Writes workouts (Activity rings via Watch), reads/writes bodyweight & body fat, imports nutrition (calories, macros) from apps like MyFitnessPal/Lose It. Not retroactive. Android: Health Connect (Strong 6.0); Google Fit dropped. Direct MyFitnessPal integration discontinued.

Apple Watch app (watchOS 10+): focus on one set/timer at a time, Digital Crown editing, set type & RPE, notes, history, heart rate & calories, rest timer; can log with or without iPhone; Live Sync mirrors the same workout on phone and watch in real time; Handoff. Not on watch: plate/warm-up calculator, focus metric, unit change. No Wear OS app.
features.user_feedback: Mature watch app praised by reviewers; but official troubleshooting pages acknowledge Live Sync issues, duplicate workouts, pairing problems and higher battery use; kg on watch rounded to .5 (2021 review).

features.how: No Garmin/Fitbit/other wearable integration in Strong's Integrations help category (only Apple Health, Health Connect, legacy MyFitnessPal).
No CSV/app import: 'exported files cannot be imported back into Strong'. (Apple Health workout/measurement imports are mentioned in 6.5.0 release notes.)

Settings > Export Strong Data → semicolon-separated CSV (Workout #, Date, Workout Name, Duration, Exercise Name, Set Order, Weight, Reps, RPE, Distance, Seconds, Notes, Workout Notes); options to include/exclude timers and notes (6.1.4); measurements CSV export (6.2.0). Free.
features.user_feedback: Export is one-way — 'an exit, not a backup' (aitoolsbakery); Hevy can import it.

features.how: Strong Cloud account sync (iPhone↔Android), background + on workout completion; force sync via pull-to-refresh (iOS) or Settings (Android). Strong 6.0 rebuilt cloud sync.
features.user_feedback: Recurring support topics: lost data from accidentally creating a second account, 'Session Expired' re-auth, disappearing templates; GGR cons cite reports of lost workouts.

features.how: iOS home-screen widgets: Workouts per Week, Calendar (monthly workouts + weekly streaks) and Activity (6.4.0). In-app Profile dashboard widgets (workouts/week, calories, macros, exercise & measurement charts).
App Store lists 'Supports Siri' and homepage lists 'Siri Shortcuts'; specific actions not documented.
No gym/location profiles documented.
Only bar type per exercise for the plate calculator (default Olympic bar; EZ bar 7.5 kg etc.); custom plate inventories not documented.
No equipment-availability filtering documented.
No social feed, followers or leaderboards — privacy-first log by design.
Share workouts/templates via link through the system share sheet; text shares include workout contents.
No leaderboards (no social features).
No challenges (no social features).
No trainer/coach product found on official pages.
Not available; trainers can only share templates by link.
Not available.
Not available.
Not available.

Free: unlimited workouts, 3 templates. PRO (US App Store): $4.99/mo (also $3.99 listed), $19.99/6 mo, $29.99/yr (also $23.99), Strong PRO Forever $99.99 (also $79.99). PRO adds unlimited templates, body-part measurements, all charts, plate & warm-up calculators, custom icons/themes. Never 'locked out' of data; no ads; no Family Sharing; gifts via store gift card.
features.user_feedback: Considered pricier than Hevy at every tier; several 2026 releases fixed PRO not unlocking without Restore Purchases.

features.how: kg or lb, 'or a combination of both'; switching units converts history. Unit change not possible on Apple Watch mid-workout (set on iPhone).
Dark mode; PRO themes and custom app icons (iPhone); Liquid Glass theme referenced in 2026 releases.
11 languages: English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Spanish (no Polish).
App Store accessibility section not filled in by developer; 6.3.0 'Improved support for the Show Borders accessibility feature'.
All users are prompted to sign up (email, Facebook or Sign in with Apple) before using Strong; a few example templates are preloaded. No goal/experience questionnaire documented.
Workouts sync to Strong Cloud 'in the background or when you complete a workout', implying local-first logging; Health Connect data stays on device. No explicit offline-mode documentation.

Account required (email/Facebook/Apple). Data stored on servers in the US and other countries, retained until account deletion (in-app). Analytics via Fathom (web) and Sentry; no personal data sent. Workouts private unless shared. App Store label: health & fitness, email, IDs linked to you; no tracking.
Per-exercise metric shown during workouts comparing to last time: Total Volume, Volume Increase (%), Weight/Rep, Total Reps, Reps/Set, Total/Average Time, Total Distance. Not on Apple Watch.
Exercise notes can be pinned so they show (yellow) every time the exercise is performed, e.g. machine settings.
features.user_feedback: Users like sticky notes for machine settings (GP reviews 2026).

features.how: Customisable Profile dashboard of widgets (workouts/week goal, calories this week, daily macros with goals, any exercise or measurement chart), reorderable by drag.
Calories and macros (protein/fat/carbs) imported from Apple Health / Google Fit nutrition apps or entered manually as Caloric Intake; goals per macro on widgets.
After a template-based workout: Update Template (red if destructive), Update Values Only, Update Template and Values, or Keep Original; can be disabled in settings.
Edit Exercise > Transfer Exercise Data merges history from one exercise into another of the same category (irreversible).
Settings > Start History From sets a date before which history is ignored in stats/records, as a non-destructive 'reset'.
Live Sync runs the same workout simultaneously on iPhone and Apple Watch; Continuity/Handoff prompts to continue a running workout on the other device.
'Strong PRO Forever' one-time purchase ($79.99/$99.99 US).
Templates can be archived instead of deleted (Archived folder).
